messages:
Maya Patel: follow-up from today's all-hands q&a. pulling the process questions into one thread so leadership can answer cleanly. please keep replies short.

Ethan Cole: two quick ones: 1) are we moving to a single org-wide release cadence? 2) what are the exact perf gates that should block a runtime rollout?

Rina Zhou: short answers: product teams default to biweekly releases; infra and runtime teams should use weekly cycles for low-risk patches and staged rollouts for risky infra changes. weekly canaries remain an option for fast feedback.

Rina Zhou: perf gates to enforce in PRs touching serving: include bench artifacts and block if p95 latency regresses >10% OR memory per request increases >15% on identical load profiles. attach baseline + branch runs.

Samir Khatri: oncall follow-up: primary rotation stays 1 week, secondary 2 weeks. we're trialing a single Monday handoff message in #eng-oncall at 09:00 PT that includes runbook links and recent pager context.

Ethan Cole: customer question from PMs: what latency guidance do we publish for Dedicated plans and are fallbacks automatic?

Maya Patel: Dedicated customers have contractual p95 latency targets. as guidance we'll publish examples: small-seq p95 <= 200ms; long-context p95 <= 500-600ms depending on model. automatic fallback chains (model_variant -> region -> degraded_variant) are enabled for critical routes by default. we'll add a short SLA FAQ entry.

OncallBot: reminder: update runbook after each handoff (template link posted in #eng-oncall).

Maya Patel: planning a 30-min follow-up office hours tomorrow 11:00 PT to walk through release patterns, the PR checklist, and the oncall handoff wording. I'll post notes + action items afterwards. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
